title: Morning routine
transcript: I've been trying to figure out why some sentences feel easy when I read them, but fall apart when I hear them. This morning I listened to the same line three times. I knew every word on the page. Still, the middle clause vanished in the audio. That gap is what I want to record, not my quiz score.

title: Coffee shop order
transcript: Yesterday I ordered coffee and the barista asked something I did not catch. She said it quickly, and the words blended together. When I read the menu aloud at home, the sentence made perfect sense. In the shop, I only heard the last word. I tagged it as sound, not vocabulary.

title: Meeting email
transcript: My colleague sent a short email about moving the meeting. The first sentence was clear. Then there was a long phrase with two verbs and I lost the subject. Reading it slowly, I see who did what. Listening to the notification read aloud, the structure collapsed. That is the pattern I need to notice.
